evidence_items.source_quote: However, the Schistosoma serology titer showed a marked elevation.

rationale: A 13-year-old male presenting with acute transverse myelitis following travel to southern Saudi Arabia. Schistosoma serology showed marked titer elevation. Symptoms and MRI findings completely resolved after experimental antischistosomal therapy. Valid positive diagnosis of neuroschistosomiasis satisfied.

evidence_items.source_quote: The results from endoscopic examination first observed egg nodes within the submucous section of colon (see Figure 2).

rationale: A 75-year-old female presenting with advanced schistosomiasis japonica. Endoscopy revealed characteristic schistosomal egg nodes within the colonic submucosa, accompanied by characteristic fish-scale liver ultrasound and portal hypertension. Confirmatory clinical diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: This time, an extensive search for parasites in stool microscopy was done and eggs of S. mansoni were identified on stool microscopy.

rationale: A 42-year-old male with visceral leishmaniasis and true coinfection with Schistosoma mansoni. Stool microscopy demonstrated eggs of S. mansoni (E1 confirmatory), and the patient received praziquantel therapy. VPD criteria satisfied.

evidence_items.source_quote: Also seen are multiple granulomas with calcified ova of S. haematobium with their characteristic terminal spines, features consistent with bilateral ectopic gestation with Schistosoma induced salpingitis.

rationale: A 32-year-old female presenting with ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Histopathology of fallopian tubes revealed granulomas with calcified ova of S. haematobium with terminal spines causing schistosomal salpingitis, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathology reported that numerous non-caseating granulomas formed of bilharzial ova (Schistosoma mansoni) and multinucleated giant cells (Figure 3).

rationale: A 10-year-old male child presenting with a large colonic mass mimicking cancer. Histopathology of the resected sigmoid demonstrated non-caseating granulomas formed of bilharzial ova (Schistosoma mansoni), treated with praziquantel with complete symptom resolution. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Titers of an indirect hemagglutination test for Schistosoma mansoni were 1:80.

rationale: A 25-year-old traveler returning from Senegal with acute Katayama fever, marked eosinophilia, and pulmonary infiltrates following freshwater exposure. Indirect hemagglutination test for Schistosoma mansoni was positive at 1:80, treated with praziquantel. E2 highly specific evidence in traveler with acute schistosomiasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histology of the excised fibrosed ureters showed features of severe schistosomiasis [Figure 7].

rationale: A 17-year-old male with severe bilateral ureteric strictures. Histology of the excised ureters confirmed features of severe schistosomiasis, and the patient received praziquantel therapy. Confirmatory E1 histopathology.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool Examination revealed ova of S. mansoni and Trophozoite stages of E. histolytica.

rationale: A 12-year-old male with bloody diarrhea and acute hepatitis coinfected with S. mansoni and E. histolytica. Stool examination identified S. mansoni ova (E1), and rectal biopsy confirmed colon/rectum schistosomiasis with Schistosoma eggs and giant cell reaction. VPD fully met.

evidence_items.source_quote: The appendix specimen was sent for histopathology and the result came back as extensive necrosis of the appendix with multiple viable Schistosomal ova (Fig. 3).

rationale: A 36-year-old male presenting with acute appendicitis. Histopathology of the appendix revealed extensive necrosis with multiple viable Schistosomal ova, and the patient was treated with praziquantel. E1 confirmatory diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: All results were negative and do not showed acute infection, except schistosoma with IgM and IgG positive.

rationale: A 45-year-old male with a retroperitoneal mass mimicking a paraganglioma. Serological evaluation was positive for Schistosoma with IgM and IgG, and treatment with praziquantel led to remission of the retroperitoneal lesion. E2 strong evidence confirmed.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological examination of the spinal cord lesion showed necrotising granulomatous chronic inflammation with Schistosoma eggs and no evidence of malignancy [Figure 3].

rationale: A 5-year-old boy presenting with acute conus medullaris paraparesis. Histopathology of the biopsied spinal cord lesion showed necrotizing granulomatous chronic inflammation with Schistosoma eggs. Treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 neuroschistosomiasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histology of the appendix showed transmural chronic fibrotic granulomatous inflammation around dead and viable schistosoma ova of both Schistosoma mansoni and Schistosoma hematobium [Figures 1 and 2].
evidence_items.target_concept: Schistosoma mansoni and Schistosoma hematobium ova

rationale: A 32-year-old male presenting with an appendiceal mass. Appendectomy histopathology showed transmural chronic fibrotic granulomatous inflammation around viable and dead schistosoma ova of S. mansoni and S. hematobium, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis was confirmed by the presence of Schistosoma heamatobium eggs in direct examination of fresh urine collected (Fig. 2).

rationale: A 27-year-old male presenting with urinary schistosomiasis. Diagnosis confirmed by presence of Schistosoma haematobium eggs in direct urine microscopy and bladder biopsy showing granulomas with bilharzia eggs. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: At high-power view, histology revealed numerous schistosome ova with terminal spines, characteristic of Schistosoma haematobium.

rationale: A 28-year-old European woman presenting with genital schistosomiasis. Cervical biopsy histopathology revealed numerous schistosome ova with terminal spines characteristic of S. haematobium containing viable miracidia, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: S. haematobium eggs appeared as bright structures (figure 1a), and after focus adjustment the characteristic egg shape and typical terminal spine became visible (figure 1b).
evidence_items.test_name: Confocal laser scanning microscopy of bladder mucosa

rationale: A 52-year-old male presenting with dysuria due to urinary schistosomiasis. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) in vivo demonstrated characteristic S. haematobium eggs with terminal spines in bladder mucosa, supported by positive ELISA serology. E1 confirmatory diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Urine microscopy showed eggs of Schistosoma haematobium, which is oval in shape and has a spiked end (Video 1).

rationale: A 14-year-old boy presenting with recurrent gross hematuria following travel to South Africa. Urine microscopy demonstrated oval eggs of Schistosoma haematobium with characteristic terminal spiked ends. Treated with praziquantel with complete resolution. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Numerous calcified Schistosoma eggs are noted (Figure 2: D-E-F)).

rationale: A 49-year-old male with severe hematuria and epithelioid angiosarcoma of the bladder. Histopathology of radical cystectomy confirmed extensive schistosomiasis with numerous calcified Schistosoma eggs in the bladder wall. Active comorbidity / true coinfection.

evidence_items.source_quote: At follow up, the wound was healing well with no surgical complications, histopathology showed periappendiceal necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with calcified parasitic ova, consistent with schistosomiasis (Fig. 3, Fig. 4).

rationale: A 31-year-old male with an Amyand hernia containing an inflamed appendix. Histopathology showed periappendiceal necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with calcified parasitic Schistosoma ova. Patient was referred to infectious diseases for treatment. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: A spinal cord biopsy was completed and confirmed the diagnosis of spinal cord schistosomiasis.

rationale: A 27-year-old male presenting with acute transverse myelopathy. Spinal cord biopsy confirmed spinal cord schistosomiasis, supported by high Schistosoma serology titer (1:64). Confirmatory E1 histopathology.

evidence_items.source_quote: His Schistosoma serology titer was high (1 : 1024).

rationale: A 65-year-old male presenting with acute abdomen from megacolon. Histopathology of resected colon demonstrated chronic schistosomiasis in the colonic wall, supported by a high Schistosoma serology titer (1:1024). E1 histopathology + E2 serology.

evidence_items.source_quote: when the final pathology confirmed conus medullaris schistosomiasis, the patient underwent subsequent treatment with praziquantel (20 mg/kg) [Figure 2].

rationale: A 6-year-old child presenting with acute myelopathy. Histopathological analysis confirmed conus medullaris schistosomiasis, and the patient was treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: chronic inflammatory schistosomal fibrosing reaction, with the presence of numerous viable eggs of the parasite in the peritoneum jejunal lesions.

rationale: A 52-year-old male liver transplant recipient. Peritoneal jejunal biopsy revealed chronic inflammatory schistosomal fibrosing reaction with numerous viable eggs of the parasite, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: A few days into his hospitalization, his Schistosoma antibody (IgG) titer was reported at at 1 : 80.

rationale: A 36-year-old Kenyan male with longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) refractory to steroids and plasmapheresis. Schistosoma antibody IgG titer was positive at 1:80 following prolonged pond swimming, and the patient was treated with praziquantel. E2 highly specific evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: study showed simultaneous squamous cell, transitional cell carcinoma (superficial type), and S. haematobium (Fig. 2 and 3), and then patient treated classically for bladder cancer (TUR-T, locally chemotherapy) and schistosomiasis (Praziquantel).

rationale: A 62-year-old male with bladder tumors. Bladder biopsy histopathology demonstrated simultaneous transitional cell carcinoma and Schistosoma haematobium eggs, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serology was eventually positive for schistosomiasis (IgE 556) and treatment was started (Praziquantel) with an interval of two weeks in between doses.

rationale: A 27-year-old male immigrant presenting with migrating pulmonary nodules. Serology was confirmed positive for schistosomiasis (IgE 556), and treatment with praziquantel resulted in complete clinical and radiological resolution. E2 highly specific evidence satisfied.

evidence_items.source_quote: uncountable, embryonated and occasionally calcified eggs of Schistosoma mansoni within the wall (most prominent in the submucosal layer) and serosa of the gastrointestinal tract.

rationale: A 24-year-old male with severe fatal schistosomiasis. Autopsy and histological analysis demonstrated uncountable embryonated eggs of Schistosoma mansoni in the gastrointestinal tract and pulmonary peribronchial vessels with eosinophilic granulomatous reaction. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: chronic jejunal inflammation with ulcerative changes and old S. japonicum eggs deposition (Figures 11 and 12).

rationale: A 65-year-old male with jejunal ulcer. Enteroscopy and histological examination confirmed chronic jejunal inflammation with deposition of Schistosoma japonicum eggs and signs of hepatic schistosomiasis. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Schistosoma serology was positive and there was an eosinophilic polynuclear leukocytosis.

rationale: A 48-year-old traveler presenting with a solitary pulmonary nodule and peripheral eosinophilia. Schistosoma serology was positive, and praziquantel therapy led to serological normalization and radiographic regression of the pulmonary nodule. E2 highly specific evidence in traveler.

evidence_items.source_quote: In the case reported, the clinical, epidemiological and histopathological conditions confirm the diagnosis of cutaneous ectopic schistosomiasis.

rationale: A 27-year-old female presenting with cutaneous papular lesions. Histopathology confirmed cutaneous ectopic schistosomiasis with identification of Schistosoma mansoni eggs, and lesions resolved following praziquantel therapy. E1 confirmatory.

evidence_items.source_quote: Manual urine microscopy on a centrifuged urine sample confirmed the diagnosis of S. hematobium infection.

rationale: A 5-year-old girl presenting with gross hematuria following travel to an endemic area. Centrifuged manual urine microscopy confirmed S. haematobium infection with characteristic parasite eggs. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: The final pathological diagnosis was colonic schistosomiasis associated with Crohn's disease.

rationale: A 35-year-old male with Crohn disease and colonic schistosomiasis. Colon resection histopathology confirmed submucosal Schistosoma eggs with terminal spines surrounded by chronic inflammatory infiltrate. Confirmatory E1 active comorbidity.

evidence_items.source_quote: The following mucosal biopsy confirmed the presence of S. japonicum eggs in the lamina propria of the rectum (Figure 2B).

rationale: A 44-year-old male presenting with a brainstem pseudotumoral lesion. Serum IgG was positive for S. japonicum, and rectal mucosal biopsy confirmed the presence of S. japonicum eggs in the lamina propria. Patient was treated with praziquantel. E1 confirmatory diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Arrows are pointing to numerous eggs in the stroma of the colonic mucosa, surrounded by eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate. The eggs are large and have a characteristic shape, with a prominent lateral spine.
evidence_items.target_concept: Schistosoma mansoni eggs with lateral spine

rationale: A 49-year-old Brazilian male presenting with esophageal varices, portal fibrosis, and a colonic polyp. Histopathology of the polyp demonstrated numerous eggs in the colonic stroma with prominent lateral spines surrounded by eosinophilic infiltrate, pathognomonic for Schistosoma mansoni. E1 confirmatory.

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis of schistosomiasis was based solely on the demonstration of eggs and adult worm in the granuloma supplied for histopathology review [Figure 4], and later confirmed by positivity in serological tests hemagglutination

rationale: A 13-year-old female presenting with a spinal cord lesion and paraparesis. Histopathology demonstrated Schistosoma eggs and adult worm within the granuloma, and hemagglutination serology was positive. E1 confirmatory medullary neuroschistosomiasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: hyperplastic polyp with multiple focal granuloma formation surrounding S. mansoni eggs, which were characterized by prominent lateral spine in the lamina propria and submucosa of the colonic wall with surrounding fibrosis (Fig. 2a-c).
evidence_items.target_concept: Schistosoma mansoni eggs with lateral spine

rationale: A 49-year-old female immigrant presenting with a colonic polyp. Biopsy demonstrated multiple focal granulomas surrounding S. mansoni eggs with prominent lateral spines, and serum Schistosoma IgG (MAMA) was markedly elevated at 2.98. Treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology report however showed a left ureteric mass with numerous Schistosoma ova within the ureteric wall (Figure 3).

rationale: A 38-year-old male with recurrent ureteric obstruction. Histopathology of the resected ureteric mass showed numerous Schistosoma ova within the ureteric wall, and the patient was retreated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology of the gallbladder showed chronic cholecystitis, with granulomatous inflammation secondary to schistosomiasis (Figure 2).

rationale: A 46-year-old male presenting with acute cholecystitis complicated by liver abscess. Histopathology of the gallbladder confirmed chronic cholecystitis with granulomatous inflammation secondary to schistosomiasis. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Unexpectedly, this demonstrated adult schistosome worms within the pulmonary vessels and eggs with a florid granulomatous inflammatory reaction within the interstitium (Fig. 2).

rationale: A 35-year-old male presenting with pulmonary nodules mimicking IgG4-related disease. Surgical lung biopsy unexpectedly revealed adult schistosome worms within pulmonary vessels and eggs with granulomatous reaction, and stool microscopy confirmed S. mansoni ova. Praziquantel led to resolution. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: Close examination of the eggs showed the terminal spine consistent with S. haematobium; the eggs was not calcified (see Figures 1, 2, and 3), indicating active inflammation.
evidence_items.target_concept: Schistosoma haematobium eggs with terminal spine

rationale: A 9-year-old boy presenting with scrotal swelling and testicular atrophy. Histopathology of thickened tunica albuginea showed active granulomatous inflammation with numerous uncalcified S. haematobium eggs bearing characteristic terminal spines. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Repeat colonoscopy revealed multiple nodular lesions in the ascending colon and cecum (Figure 1(b)), and the biopsy revealed intramucosal Schistosoma mansoni eggs surrounded by chronic inflammatory cells, including eosinophils.

rationale: A 26-year-old male with chronic diarrhea and abdominal pain. Colonoscopic biopsy confirmed intramucosal Schistosoma mansoni eggs surrounded by eosinophilic and chronic inflammatory cells, accompanied by periportal fibrosis on ultrasound. Treated with praziquantel with rapid clinical response. Confirmatory E1.

evidence_items.source_quote: parasitic eggs and gliosis, morphologically consistent with Schistosoma eggs (Figure 3).

rationale: A 38-year-old male presenting with a brain lesion. Histopathology of stereotactic brain biopsy demonstrated parasitic eggs and gliosis morphologically consistent with Schistosoma eggs, treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Zeil-Neelson (ZN) staining was consistent with S. mansoni ova (Figure 5). A diagnosis of chronic schistosomiasis of the vulva was made. The lesion resolved with the administration of oral praziquantel.

rationale: A 37-year-old female presenting with persistent vulvar itch and nodular lesion. Biopsy histopathology and Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrated Schistosoma mansoni ova with characteristic lateral spines. Diagnosis of chronic vulvar schistosomiasis was confirmed and resolved with oral praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: A Schistosoma genus polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of the pericardial tissue was positive for Schistosoma species, but could not differentiate between S. haematobium and S. mansoni.

rationale: A 71-year-old female presenting with pericardial effusion and B-cell lymphoma. Pericardial biopsy showed non-caseating granulomatous inflammation surrounding Schistosoma haematobium ova, and pericardial PCR was positive for Schistosoma species. Treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Bronchoalveolar lavage from posterobasal segment of right lower lobe was sent for investigation, which was suggestive of parasitic infection Schistosoma haematobium.

rationale: A 27-year-old immunocompromised male presenting with pulmonary infiltrates. Bronchoalveolar lavage wet mount and repeat sputum examination confirmed Schistosoma haematobium infection, and the patient was successfully treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological examination of removed tissues revealed the presence of chorionic villi, abundant triploblastic proliferation and calcified Schistosoma eggs (Figure 2(a) and (b)).

rationale: A 35-year-old female presenting with ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Histological examination of excised fallopian tissues revealed calcified Schistosoma eggs within chorionic villi, and the patient completed 6 weeks of praziquantel therapy. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytology revealed Schistosoma haematobium eggs in a hemorrhagic and suppurative background with no malignant features.

rationale: An 11-year-old girl presenting with recurrent gross hematuria. Urine cytology and bladder biopsy histopathology confirmed Schistosoma haematobium ova with giant-cell reaction, treated with praziquantel with complete resolution. Confirmatory E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Following the detection of S. haematobium in the urine parasitology test, the patient was transferred to the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Department on 01/09.

rationale: A 16-year-old male migrant presenting with hematuria. Centrifuged urine parasitology examination confirmed S. haematobium eggs with terminal spines, and the patient was treated with praziquantel. Confirmatory E1 evidence.
